title: Why a work message can feel like a threat

narration: Before you reach the second line,
beats.visual_intent: a worker at her desk; a glowing envelope marked urgent drops in, and a jagged burst flares behind her as her heart starts to race

grounding.claim: the worker and her message are an invented illustration
a perceived threat sets off a fast response

narration: It gets you ready to act.
beats.visual_intent: we move inside her: a glowing core switches on in her chest, and the term arrives on a label pinned to it

grounding.claim: the fast stress response prepares the body for action

beats.visual_intent: the adrenaline label pins to her body, the core beats faster and electricity runs along her outline as energy reaches her arms

grounding.claim: adrenaline raises heart rate and breathing and releases energy for the muscles

beats.visual_intent: a second label, cortisol, pins beside the first; the glow holds steady instead of fading

grounding.claim: cortisol keeps energy available while the threat seems to last

beats.visual_intent: a status panel of her body's jobs; each one switches off on its spoken word, one at a time

grounding.claim: non-urgent functions such as digestion are turned down
acute stress can make careful thinking harder

narration: Something to fight, or run from.
beats.visual_intent: a wide, living place long ago: a figure in the open as a large shadow passes; the alarm makes sense here

grounding.claim: the response evolved for short physical dangers

narration: But the same alarm goes off
beats.visual_intent: back to today: the day's pressures circle her and close in, a calendar, a chat, an envelope, each arriving on its word

grounding.claim: psychological pressures can set off the same response

recall.prompt: so is the racing heart a fault?

narration: So that racing heart is not a fault.
It is the alarm, doing its job.
beats.visual_intent: the circling pressures fall away; she stands lit and steady, one short line to hold on to

grounding.claim: a stress response in the moment is normal

beats.misconception: a strong reaction means I am overreacting

narration: The alarm settles on its own,
but it takes a little time.
beats.visual_intent: a gauge beside her slides from alarm down to calm while the glow in her chest softens

grounding.claim: the calming system brings arousal down, which takes some time

beats.visual_intent: the opening desk again, now calm: the envelope arrives, a small pause, and the reply goes out; three steps light up in turn

grounding.claim: the worker is an invented illustration
pausing before acting on a strong reaction can make an impulsive reply less likely
